_why: The probe I should have run before spending a 20-generation building kit. Raheem's reference cliffs are organic and lobed; shape_style 'round' plus high raggedness is the parameter pair built for exactly that, and slope_size gives the wall height the building kit was supposed to provide.
_probe: ONE call, look at it, THEN decide. No reference image yet because Raheem's screenshot is not on disk — this is testing whether the procedural shape controls alone get near it.
lower_description: sandy dirt ground, warm tan, flat and open
upper_description: raised rocky plateau top, warm brown packed earth with tufts of grass and scattered stones
transition_description: a natural rock cliff face dropping from the plateau to the ground, rounded lobed boulders and strata, warm brown and grey-brown stone, darker in the shadow at its foot
_shape_style: REJECTED with 422: 'shape_style cannot be combined with mode=pro'. Kept pro and dropped shape_style, because pro is the mode that carries raggedness (the lobed boundary noise) AND slope_size (the wall height) — the two things the reference actually needs. shape_style='round' is only available on standard, which has neither. The 422 cost nothing: validation fires before any generation.
